alternative_queries: Context-aware learning-to-rank for recommendation using impression-time tab, hour, and weekday features: compare additive scorers, factorization machines, and lightweight feature-interaction architectures under sparse and cold-start conditions; evaluate within-user GAUC and nDCG@5 while excluding post-impression outcomes and unavailable aggregate snapshots.

Feature interaction methods for context-aware recommender systems with request-time categorical context such as tab, hour, and weekday, focusing on whether factorization machines, field-aware interactions, or compact cross layers improve ranking over additive user/item models for sparse users and items; report GAUC and nDCG@5 without leakage from current-impression behavior.

Architectures for incorporating available impression-time context into recommendation ranking models, comparing linear or additive models with factorization machines, polynomial interaction models, embeddings, and lightweight cross features; study tab-specific performance, cold-start robustness, and within-user GAUC and nDCG@5 using only features available before or at impression time.

Context-aware recommendation and sparse feature-interaction modeling for ranking: effects of interactions between user, item, tab, hour, and weekday in additive versus factorization-machine or other low-parameter architectures, with emphasis on severe segment weaknesses, cold-start users/items, implementation cost, GAUC, and nDCG@5; exclude post-impression labels and response aggregates.

Impression-time contextual ranking for recommender systems under data sparsity: literature comparing additive user/video scorers with factorization machines and lightweight interaction mechanisms for tab-, temporal-, and user/item-context interactions, including trade-offs in coverage, training complexity, and deployment latency, evaluated with within-user GAUC and top-five nDCG while preventing outcome leakage.

robust recommender systems under exposure bias, domain shift, and context shift; compare shared global models, tab/channel-specific models, fallback rankers, and mixture-of-experts; evaluate subgroup robustness with fixed within-user temporal splits, GAUC, and nDCG@5 while excluding impression-time outcome leakage

recommendation ranking failures across tabs, channels, or request contexts under temporal distribution shift; evidence for context-aware treatment, shared representations, hierarchical models, and fallback ranking; subgroup evaluation using GAUC and nDCG@5 with impression-time feature availability and no current-impression outcome leakage

mixture-of-experts and fallback models for robust recommendation under heterogeneous exposure contexts and domain shift; analyze weak tab-specific ranking performance and when to specialize versus share parameters; use fixed within-user chronological evaluation, train-only feature construction, GAUC, nDCG@5, and subgroup robustness metrics

context-aware recommender evaluation under exposure and population heterogeneity, including tab/channel effects, cold or sparse subgroups, and negative-slice diagnosis; compare additive shared scorers, context-specific models, and fallback strategies using temporally consistent within-user validation, GAUC, and nDCG@5 without leakage from current impressions

literature on subgroup-robust learning-to-rank and recommendation under context shift and exposure bias; methods for detecting and mitigating tab-specific GAUC and top-five nDCG degradation through shared models, experts, gating, or fallbacks; require fixed within-user temporal holdouts, impression-time covariates only, and evaluation with GAUC and nDCG@5
